builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
summary: This method replaces the full-rank erase and write gates in Gated DeltaNet-2 with a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection and a matched-filter readout gate. It requires implementing a novel parallel chunkwise update algorithm to maintain numerical stability during training, which introduces significant engineering complexity and risk. The technique has only been validated at 1.34B parameters; it is unproven at the larger scales typically required for production foundation models, and custom kernels may not be available or optimized for consumer-grade 24GB GPUs.
rationale: While the architecture offers theoretical efficiency and quality gains, it requires training new foundation models from scratch, which exceeds the reader's constrained infrastructure and budget.

claims.statement: This method replaces the full-rank erase and write gates in Gated DeltaNet-2 with a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection and a matched-filter readout gate. It requires implementing a novel parallel chunkwise update algorithm to maintain numerical stability during training, which introduces significant engineering complexity and risk. The technique has only been validated at 1.34B parameters; it is unproven at the larger scales typically required for production foundation models, and custom kernels may not be available or optimized for consumer-grade 24GB GPUs.
At 1.34B parameters, Muir lowers perplexity by 1.8-2.0% over GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% over Transformer, while matching GDN-2 throughput and training 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K context.
